definition: Secret Management is a core concept in .NET Full Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Secret Management is
theory.body: Secret Management describes the methods and patterns used within .NET Full Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Secret Management is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Secret Management matters
theory.body: Without Secret Management, systems built with .NET Full Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Secret Management works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Secret Management follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Secret Management.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Secret Management
theory.body: Secret Management offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
